title: Swap Thrashing Detection
exclusions: Detects sustained, host-level bidirectional Linux swap traffic with corroborating system-wide memory-pressure stall time. It does not identify the responsible process or cgroup, distinguish anonymous-memory owners, prove that swap caused an application SLO breach, cover hosts without both `/proc/vmstat` and `/proc/pressure/memory`, or establish regulatory compliance. It does not use the Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux `vmstat` event as though that event contained native `si` and `so` fields.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `linux_swap_thrashing_5m` saved-search definition, dispatch history, alert results, and dashboard exports containing `host`, `boot_id`, `window_start`, `window_end`, `avg_swapin_kib_s`, `avg_swapout_kib_s`, `avg_psi_full_stall_pct`, `max_psi_some_stall_pct`, `swap_buckets`, and `impact_buckets`. These artifacts demonstrate configured monitoring and observed signals; they do not by themselves prove root cause, production validation, or compliance.

controlTest.positiveScenario: For `host=swap-positive`, index six one-minute `linux:swap_psi` events under one `boot_id` with `page_size_bytes=4096`. Increase both `pswpin_pages` and `pswpout_pages` by 30,720 pages between every adjacent pair (2,048 KiB/s for 60 seconds), and increase `psi_full_total_us` by 9,000,000 microseconds (15 percent full memory stall) and `psi_some_total_us` by at least that amount. The five derived candidate buckets must produce one result with `observed_buckets=5`, `swap_buckets=5`, `psi_buckets=5`, and `impact_buckets=5`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Repeat the same six-event, bidirectional 2,048 KiB/s swap sequence for `host=swap-negative`, but keep `psi_full_total_us` unchanged. The search must return no result because sustained swap traffic without corroborating full memory stall does not satisfy this thrashing policy. Separately decrease either cumulative swap counter or change `boot_id`; the affected interval must be discarded rather than converted into a negative or wrapped rate.

dataSources: `index=os sourcetype=linux:swap_psi source=linux_swap_psi` events from a deployment-owned Universal Forwarder scripted input that reads cumulative `pswpin` and `pswpout` page counters from `/proc/vmstat`, system page size from `getconf PAGE_SIZE`, boot identity from `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, and `some`/`full` cumulative microsecond totals from `/proc/pressure/memory`. Required cadence is 60 seconds. The standard `Splunk_TA_nix` `vmstat.sh` event is optional context only: on Linux it runs `vmstat -s` and exposes cumulative `pgSwapOut`, but it does not supply the bidirectional `si`/`so` pair required here.
app: A deployment-owned scripted-input app (example name `TA_linux_swap_psi`) on Linux Universal Forwarders. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (`Splunk_TA_nix`, Splunkbase 833) is optional for adjacent memory, process, and CPU context, not the primary detector feed.

spl:
index=os sourcetype=linux:swap_psi source=linux_swap_psi host=* earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval pswpin_pages=tonumber(pswpin_pages), pswpout_pages=tonumber(pswpout_pages), page_size_bytes=tonumber(page_size_bytes), psi_some_total_us=tonumber(psi_some_total_us), psi_full_total_us=tonumber(psi_full_total_us)
| where isnotnull(pswpin_pages) AND isnotnull(pswpout_pages) AND isnotnull(page_size_bytes) AND page_size_bytes>0 AND isnotnull(boot_id)
| stats max(pswpin_pages) as pswpin_pages max(pswpout_pages) as pswpout_pages max(psi_some_total_us) as psi_some_total_us max(psi_full_total_us) as psi_full_total_us max(page_size_bytes) as page_size_bytes by host boot_id _time
| sort 0 host boot_id _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(pswpin_pages) as previous_pswpin_pages last(pswpout_pages) as previous_pswpout_pages last(psi_some_total_us) as previous_psi_some_total_us last(psi_full_total_us) as previous_psi_full_total_us last(_time) as previous_time by host boot_id
| eval elapsed_seconds=_time-previous_time
| eval swapin_delta_pages=if(pswpin_pages>=previous_pswpin_pages,pswpin_pages-previous_pswpin_pages,null()), swapout_delta_pages=if(pswpout_pages>=previous_pswpout_pages,pswpout_pages-previous_pswpout_pages,null())
| eval psi_some_delta_us=if(psi_some_total_us>=previous_psi_some_total_us,psi_some_total_us-previous_psi_some_total_us,null()), psi_full_delta_us=if(psi_full_total_us>=previous_psi_full_total_us,psi_full_total_us-previous_psi_full_total_us,null())
| eval swapin_kib_s=if(elapsed_seconds>0 AND elapsed_seconds<=150,swapin_delta_pages*page_size_bytes/1024/elapsed_seconds,null()), swapout_kib_s=if(elapsed_seconds>0 AND elapsed_seconds<=150,swapout_delta_pages*page_size_bytes/1024/elapsed_seconds,null())
| eval psi_some_stall_pct=if(elapsed_seconds>0 AND elapsed_seconds<=150,100*psi_some_delta_us/(elapsed_seconds*1000000),null()), psi_full_stall_pct=if(elapsed_seconds>0 AND elapsed_seconds<=150,100*psi_full_delta_us/(elapsed_seconds*1000000),null())
| where isnotnull(swapin_kib_s) AND isnotnull(swapout_kib_s)
| bin _time span=1m
| stats avg(swapin_kib_s) as swapin_kib_s avg(swapout_kib_s) as swapout_kib_s avg(psi_some_stall_pct) as psi_some_stall_pct avg(psi_full_stall_pct) as psi_full_stall_pct latest(page_size_bytes) as page_size_bytes count as rate_samples count(psi_full_stall_pct) as psi_rate_samples by host boot_id _time
| eval candidate_start=relative_time(now(),"-10m@m"), candidate_end=relative_time(now(),"-5m@m"), swap_threshold_kib_s=1024, psi_full_threshold_pct=10
| where _time>=candidate_start AND _time<candidate_end
| eval swap_breach=if(swapin_kib_s>=swap_threshold_kib_s AND swapout_kib_s>=swap_threshold_kib_s,1,0), psi_present=if(psi_rate_samples>0,1,0), psi_impact=if(psi_rate_samples>0 AND psi_full_stall_pct>=psi_full_threshold_pct,1,0)
| stats count as observed_buckets sum(swap_breach) as swap_buckets sum(psi_present) as psi_buckets sum(psi_impact) as impact_buckets min(_time) as window_start max(_time) as window_end avg(swapin_kib_s) as avg_swapin_kib_s avg(swapout_kib_s) as avg_swapout_kib_s avg(psi_full_stall_pct) as avg_psi_full_stall_pct max(psi_some_stall_pct) as max_psi_some_stall_pct min(rate_samples) as min_rate_samples values(page_size_bytes) as page_size_bytes by host boot_id
| where observed_buckets=5 AND swap_buckets=5 AND psi_buckets=5 AND impact_buckets>=3
| eval window_end=window_end+60, avg_swapin_kib_s=round(avg_swapin_kib_s,1), avg_swapout_kib_s=round(avg_swapout_kib_s,1), avg_psi_full_stall_pct=round(avg_psi_full_stall_pct,2), max_psi_some_stall_pct=round(max_psi_some_stall_pct,2), severity="critical"
| sort 0 -avg_psi_full_stall_pct -avg_swapout_kib_s
description: Reports a Linux host only when five consecutive closed one-minute buckets each average at least 1,024 KiB/s in both swap directions and at least three of those buckets show 10 percent or more full memory-pressure stall time. The search derives rates from adjacent cumulative kernel counters, converts pages with the host's measured page size, separates boots, and rejects long collection gaps or counter decreases.
value: Sustained swap-in and swap-out can turn memory shortage into repeated disk work, but swap traffic alone does not prove user-visible harm. Correlating it with Linux full memory-pressure stall time focuses paging on hosts where all non-idle work is losing productive time and shortens triage toward workload reduction, leak investigation, or capacity action.
implementation: Deploy a small, reviewed scripted-input app to each in-scope Linux Universal Forwarder. Collect `/proc/vmstat`, `/proc/pressure/memory`, page size, and boot ID every 60 seconds into `index=os sourcetype=linux:swap_psi`; install matching search-time key-value extraction. Save `linux_swap_thrashing_5m`, schedule it every five minutes, and retain the explicit closed-window bounds. Treat 1,024 KiB/s per direction for five minutes plus at least three minutes at 10 percent full PSI as an initial policy to baseline by host class, not a Linux or Splunk default.
visualization: Create a per-host timechart with `swapin_kib_s` and `swapout_kib_s` on a KiB/s axis and `psi_full_stall_pct` on a separate percent axis; add horizontal policy lines at 1,024 KiB/s and 10 percent. Provide a current-results table with all evidence fields and drilldowns to process RSS/swap, cgroup pressure, major faults, block-device latency, OOM events, and changes. Never chart cumulative `pswpin_pages`, `pswpout_pages`, or PSI `total` values as rates.
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM-accelerated equivalent is asserted. The required cumulative `/proc/vmstat` swap-in/swap-out counters, boot identity, page size, and PSI cumulative stall totals are source-specific and are not a normalized CIM Performance dataset contract. A `tstats` search over generic memory capacity fields cannot preserve this detector's delta, unit, reset, gap, and impact semantics.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Planned swap-path or memory-pressure load test** — A controlled `stress-ng --vm` exercise can satisfy both swap and PSI gates by design. Match the exact host and test window to an approved change, retain the result as test evidence, and suppress only notification delivery for that interval.

2. **Hibernate or suspend preparation** — Systems configured to write memory state to swap can generate intense page-out activity, although ordinary server fleets rarely hibernate. Correlate with systemd sleep targets and power-management logs; exclude only hosts whose documented role includes hibernation.

3. **Cold-start fan-in after reboot or failover** — Simultaneous service startup can fault recently swapped pages in while new processes force other pages out. The `boot_id` prevents a cross-reboot counter delta, but a real post-boot pressure episode can still satisfy the policy. Correlate with boot time, orchestrator placement, and service readiness before paging a workload owner.

4. **Memory overcommit or ballooning drill on virtual machines** — A sanctioned hypervisor reclamation test can create genuine guest full stalls and bidirectional swap. Confirm the VM, reservation change, and drill ticket; do not label the detector false at the signal level, only expected operationally.

5. **Host-class threshold mismatch** — 1 MiB/s can be material on a small latency-sensitive node and routine on a large batch host with fast swap. Baseline web, database, batch, and virtual-desktop hosts separately; preserve the five-bucket and PSI impact requirements while changing the rate floor through reviewed policy.

6. **Duplicate collectors or host-name collision** — Two forwarders reporting different machines under one `host` can produce counter jumps. `boot_id` reduces this risk, but duplicate events can still distort bucket averages. Compare `source`, `splunk_server`, forwarder GUID, and event counts before treating an extreme rate as kernel behavior.

**Suppression mechanism:** the primary SPL intentionally contains no hidden lookup. If notification policy requires exceptions, apply a reviewed lookup after the final detection, keyed by exact `host`, `start_epoch`, and `end_epoch`, with owner, reason, ticket, and expiry. Preserve unsuppressed search results and never use permanent wildcard exclusions.

reviewer: documentation review against Linux kernel, procps-ng, and Splunk primary sources; no production execution or SME sign-off
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement contract

Assign a Linux platform owner, a Splunk content owner, and a workload escalation path. The in-scope host must expose readable `/proc/vmstat`, `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, and `/proc/pressure/memory`; the latter is the system-wide Pressure Stall Information (PSI) interface and must contain both `some` and `full` lines. Run the collector under the actual Universal Forwarder service identity before rollout. The files are normally readable without elevated write privileges, but hardened procfs mounts, containers, or host security policy can change visibility. The collector needs read access only; it must never write a PSI trigger or change `vm.swappiness`.

Understand the signal before deploying it. Linux `/proc/vmstat` publishes cumulative `pswpin` and `pswpout` counters. They are page counts, not bytes/second, so the search must subtract adjacent observations, divide by elapsed seconds, and multiply by that host's `PAGE_SIZE`. `vmstat(8)` presents `si` and `so` as memory swapped per second and allows unit selection, but those periodic columns are not fields in the standard Linux `Splunk_TA_nix` `vmstat.sh` event. The add-on's Linux script uses `vmstat -s` and exposes cumulative `pgSwapOut`; it does not provide the paired swap-in counter this UC requires. Do not search nonexistent `si`/`so` fields and do not label a raw page delta as KiB/s.

PSI provides the impact qualifier. The kernel defines `some` as time when at least some tasks are stalled and `full` as time when all non-idle tasks are stalled; extended `full` stall is specifically described as thrashing. Each line includes rolling percentages and a cumulative `total` in microseconds. This implementation deltas `total` over the exact collection interval so its percentage shares the same measurement window as the swap rates. It retains `some` for context but gates on `full`.

Create an `os` event index or substitute your approved index everywhere. `os` is a deployment convention, not a Splunk requirement. The search role needs read access to that index. Keep the deployment app and search knowledge objects under version control. This documentation review did not execute the collector or SPL on a production Splunk instance, so the UC remains community status.

## Step 1 — Configure and verify collection

Create a deployment-owned app such as `TA_linux_swap_psi`; do not modify files inside `Splunk_TA_nix`. Place the `scriptExample` in `TA_linux_swap_psi/bin/linux_swap_psi.sh`, owned by the Splunk service account and executable by that account. The script emits one line of `key=value` data and exits rather than publishing partial counters when mandatory fields are absent. Configure the Universal Forwarder with:

```ini
[script://./bin/linux_swap_psi.sh]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
source = linux_swap_psi
sourcetype = linux:swap_psi
```

On the search tier, make extraction explicit in the same app's `local/props.conf` (or a search-head companion app):

```ini
[linux:swap_psi]
KV_MODE = auto
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT
```

Splunk documents 60 seconds as the scripted-input default, but pin it explicitly because the alert's completeness policy assumes one observation per minute. The expected volume is about 1,440 short events per host per day; measure actual bytes in your environment rather than inventing a licensing estimate. On Splunk Cloud, run the script on a customer-managed Universal Forwarder and forward the events; do not claim that customer shell scripts execute on the managed search tier.

Before broad deployment, execute the script as the forwarder user. Require numeric `page_size_bytes`, `pswpin_pages`, `pswpout_pages`, `psi_some_total_us`, and `psi_full_total_us`, plus a nonempty `boot_id`. Compare page size with `getconf PAGE_SIZE`, the two counters with `awk '$1=="pswpin" || $1=="pswpout" {print}' /proc/vmstat`, and PSI totals with `cat /proc/pressure/memory`. Then verify the effective stanza with `splunk btool inputs list --debug` and search `index=os sourcetype=linux:swap_psi source=linux_swap_psi earliest=-10m | table _time host boot_id page_size_bytes pswpin_pages pswpout_pages psi_*`. Expect approximately one event per minute per host.

If `/proc/pressure/memory` is unavailable, the script emits `psi_available=0`; such a host is intentionally ineligible for the primary alert. Do not silently downgrade it to a swap-only page. Track missing PSI as a data-quality panel and either remediate kernel/namespace visibility or define a separately named, lower-confidence policy.

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_swap_thrashing_5m` and schedule it on five-minute boundaries with cron `*/5 * * * *`. Preserve `earliest=-20m@m latest=-5m@m`. The search uses the five closed minutes from ten to five minutes ago as candidates and reserves earlier events for the first adjacent delta. Excluding the newest five minutes avoids firing on a partially indexed bucket when forwarding is delayed.

### Understanding this SPL

`tonumber` makes malformed values null. The first `stats` collapses duplicate events at the same host, boot, and timestamp without summing cumulative counters. `sort 0 host boot_id _time` is mandatory because `streamstats` consumes results in order. `streamstats current=f window=1` copies the immediately preceding counters and timestamp within the same `host` and `boot_id`; therefore a reboot cannot be compared with the prior boot.

The delta expressions accept only nondecreasing counters. They divide by observed `elapsed_seconds`, not an assumed 60, and discard intervals over 150 seconds so a collection outage is not presented as a current rate. Multiplying page delta by `page_size_bytes/1024` converts pages to KiB before dividing by seconds. PSI percentage is `100 * delta_microseconds / (elapsed_seconds * 1,000,000)`. The one-minute aggregation aligns minor script jitter, and the final aggregation requires all five possible candidate buckets.

The initial policy requires both swap directions to average at least 1,024 KiB/s in every candidate bucket and full PSI to average at least 10 percent in at least three of five. These are transparent operational starting points, not kernel, procps-ng, or Splunk vendor defaults, and no single universal swap threshold exists. Full PSI supplies the impact evidence: 10 percent means all non-idle work was simultaneously stalled for roughly six seconds of a one-minute interval. Baseline by host class and application SLO. If policy values move to a lookup, make missing or expired policy rows fail closed and preserve the resolved thresholds in every alert result.

Trigger when result count is greater than zero. Notify per `host` and `boot_id`, throttle the same pair for 30 minutes, and include both rates, both PSI summaries, the five bucket counts, page size, and window times. Do not auto-kill a process, drop caches, disable swap, or change swappiness from this alert.

There is no equivalent CIM `tstats` query. Generic memory capacity fields cannot recreate the cumulative counter deltas, page-size conversion, boot reset, collection-gap rejection, or PSI impact gate.

## Step 3 — Validate units, resets, completeness, and controls

First validate one real adjacent pair manually. Compute `(new_pswpin-old_pswpin) * page_size_bytes / 1024 / elapsed_seconds` and compare it with `swapin_kib_s`; repeat for swap-out. Compute `(new_psi_full_total_us-old_psi_full_total_us) * 100 / (elapsed_seconds*1000000)` and compare it with `psi_full_stall_pct`. Do not compare the exact value with `vmstat`'s first report because `vmstat(8)` states that first report is an average since boot; use a delayed second report such as `vmstat -y 1 2` where supported and account for collection timing.

Run the positive control exactly as specified. With 4,096-byte pages, 30,720 pages over 60 seconds equals 2,048 KiB/s: `30720*4096/1024/60`. A 9,000,000-microsecond PSI full delta over 60 seconds equals 15 percent. All five candidate buckets must breach both swap floors, contain PSI, and pass the impact threshold. For the negative control, keep swap deltas identical but hold full PSI total constant; no row may survive. This distinction proves that the alert does not equate heavy swap traffic with demonstrated thrashing.

Also test: a counter decrease under the same boot ID; a changed boot ID; a gap longer than 150 seconds; one missing candidate minute; a nonnumeric value; and duplicate events. Decreases and the first observation of a new boot must produce no rate, a long gap must be discarded, fewer than five candidate buckets must not alert, malformed events must be excluded, and duplicate timestamps must not be summed.

Check cadence over 24 hours with `index=os sourcetype=linux:swap_psi earliest=-24h | timechart span=1m count by host limit=0`. Investigate missing minutes and duplicate streams. Record these deterministic search tests as documentation/control evidence only; do not call the UC production-verified until a qualified operator executes and signs off the deployed collector, search, and alert path.

## Step 4 — Operationalize and investigate

Build a dashboard with separate units. Plot derived swap-in and swap-out in KiB/s together; plot full and some PSI percentages on a percent axis; never overlay raw cumulative totals without clear labelling. Add a current-alert table and a data-quality table for missing PSI, stale hosts, duplicate collectors, counter resets, and collection gaps. Provide 30-minute, 24-hour, and 7-day views.

The runbook should first confirm all five buckets, counter continuity, boot ID, page size, and PSI presence. Next inspect application latency and errors, OOM or killed-process messages, major page faults, block-device latency, memory availability, and recent deployments. Use `smem`, `/proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup`, `systemd-cgtop`, cgroup v2 `memory.current`, `memory.events`, and per-cgroup `memory.pressure` where available to identify consumers; system-wide PSI alone cannot name one. In virtual machines, also inspect ballooning and host overcommit. Escalate to the workload owner before stopping processes or resizing.

Route confirmed results to Linux/platform on-call because the policy requires measurable full stall. Attach the exact window, rates, PSI percentages, service owner, and relevant changes. Review the rate floor and impact threshold after hardware, swap-device, kernel, memory, or workload-class changes. Retain alert and dispatch history according to operational policy, but avoid claiming those artifacts satisfy an unrelated audit requirement.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot and suppress safely

No events usually means the deployment app is absent, the input is disabled, the script is not executable, procfs is restricted, routing targets another index, or the role cannot search it. Run the script as the forwarder identity and inspect `splunkd.log` for the exact scripted-input path. Events with raw key-value text but null fields indicate the search-tier props are missing or the sourcetype differs. `psi_available=0` means the file is absent or unreadable in that namespace; it is not zero pressure.

Null rates usually mean this is the first event for a boot, timestamps duplicate or move backward, a counter decreased, or the gap exceeds 150 seconds. Implausibly large rates require checking page size, duplicate collectors, hostname collision, merged systems, timestamp lag, and counter extraction. Visible pressure with no alert can be correct when either direction is below 1,024 KiB/s, fewer than five complete swap buckets exist, fewer than five PSI buckets exist, or fewer than three buckets reach 10 percent full stall.

For approved tests or maintenance, suppress notification only after the final detection with an exact host and bounded time range. Require owner, reason, ticket, start, and expiry, and retain the unsuppressed result. Never add a broad host wildcard, permanent exception, or pre-delta event filter that can splice counters across an excluded interval.
grandmaExplanation: We watch for a Linux server repeatedly shuffling memory to and from disk while its work is being forced to wait. If that continues for several minutes, the team gets a focused warning that the machine is struggling, not merely using swap.
